catalyst_text: NDA accepted priority review PDUFA November 27 2026
detailed_catalyst_text: The FDA accepted the NDA with Priority Review for an oral therapy for limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 and set a PDUFA action date of November 27, 2026. The agency also indicated it is not currently planning to convene an advisory committee meeting. This milestone advances the program toward potential approval for a population with significant unmet need.
catalyst_text_evidence: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a commercial-stage, multi-product biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today announced the FDA has accepted for filing its New Drug Application (NDA) with Priority Review for oral BBP-418 for the treatment of individuals living with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9). The FDA has assigned a Prescription Drug User Fee Act (PDUFA) target action date of 2026-11-27, and BridgeBio is poised to launch BBP-418 upon approval. The FDA also notified the Company that it is not currently planning to hold an advisory committee meeting to discuss the application.

catalyst_text: Submitted NDA following positive Phase 3 results presentation
detailed_catalyst_text: An NDA was submitted to the FDA for treatment of autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 1. The filing is supported by Phase 3 CALIBRATE results that met all pre-specified primary and key secondary endpoints, with additional positive data presented at ECE 2026. This represents a major regulatory milestone for a potential first disease-specific therapy.
catalyst_text_evidence: PALO ALTO, Calif., 2026-05-12 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a commercial-stage, multi-product biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today announced the submission of its New Drug Application (NDA) to the FDA for encaleret as a potential targeted treatment for autosomal dominant hypocalcemia type 1 (ADH1). CALIBRATE, the Phase 3 clinical trial of encaleret in ADH1, successfully achieved all pre-specified primary and key secondary efficacy endpoints, supporting encaleret's potential as a disease-modifying therapy by targeting the underlying genetic cause of ADH1. Additional positive results were presented at the European Congress of Endocrinology (ECE) 2026 in an oral presentation, with data showing comprehensive normalization of mineral homeostasis.

catalyst_text: Presented positive Phase 3 data at ESC Heart Failure
detailed_catalyst_text: New analyses from the Phase 3 ATTRibute-CM trial were presented at ESC-HF 2026, showing increased sTTR levels and significantly reduced sTTR variability associated with lower mortality risk, plus early and sustained reductions in outpatient worsening heart failure versus placebo. An anchored matching-adjusted indirect comparison versus tafamidis showed a 34% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalizations with a favorable mortality trend, and additional posters demonstrated consistent benefits on NT-proBNP and KCCQ-OS. These results support disease-modifying effects and clinically meaningful benefit across biomarkers, symptoms, and outcomes in individuals with ATTR-CM.
catalyst_text_evidence: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. ... today announced new data from the Phase 3 ATTRibute-CM study at Heart Failure 2026, organized by the Heart Failure Association of the European Society of Cardiology (ESC-HF), further demonstrating acoramidis' consistent and clinically meaningful benefit across the transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM) disease spectrum, with new data demonstrating disease modifying effects across clinical outcomes, biomarkers, and functional capacity. In a late-breaking oral presentation shared by Senthil Selvaraj, M.D. ... acoramidis showed an association between the treatment-related increase in serum transthyretin (sTTR) and a significant reduction of sTTR variability over time, which is independently associated with reduced all-cause mortality (ACM). Acoramidis increased sTTR levels early (Day 28) and sustained them through Month 30, while significantly reducing sTTR variability versus placebo (9.5% vs. 12.8%; p<0.001). Acoramidis reduced the risk of outpatient worsening heart failure versus placebo by 41% (HR 0.59, 95% CI 0.46–0.75; p < 0.0001, with K-M curve separation seen within 30 days and sustained through Month 30). Acoramidis demonstrated a statistically significant, 34% reduction in cardiovascular hospitalizations versus tafamidis (RRR: 0.66; 95% CI: 0.46–0.95). In addition to the presentations highlighted, three additional acoramidis posters were also shared at Heart Failure 2026.

catalyst_text: Received ANVISA approval for transthyretin cardiomyopathy treatment
detailed_catalyst_text: Brazil’s health authority ANVISA granted marketing authorization for acoramidis under the brand name BEYONTTRA to treat adult patients with wild-type or variant transthyretin amyloidosis with cardiomyopathy. The decision was supported by the Phase 3 ATTRibute-CM study showing significant reductions in cardiovascular-related hospitalizations and improved survival. This approval expands access to therapy for transthyretin cardiomyopathy patients in Brazil.
catalyst_text_evidence: PALO ALTO, Calif., 2026-05-06 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a new type of biopharmaceutical company focused on genetic diseases, today announced the Brazilian Health Regulatory Agency (ANVISA) has granted marketing authorization for acoramidis, under the brand name BEYONTTRA, for the treatment of wild-type or variant transthyretin amyloidosis in adult patients with cardiomyopathy (ATTR-CM). The approval in Brazil is based on results of the pivotal ATTRibute-CM Phase 3 study of acoramidis, which showed clear benefits on cardiovascular outcomes.

catalyst_text: Submitted NDA following positive Phase 3 interim results
detailed_catalyst_text: An NDA was submitted to the FDA for an oral therapy targeting Limb-Girdle Muscular Dystrophy Type 2I/R9. The filing is supported by the Phase 3 FORTIFY 12-month interim analysis meeting all pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints with favorable safety and clinically meaningful improvements in ambulation and pulmonary function, and additional positive data were presented at the 2026 MDA conference. This represents a key regulatory milestone for a disease with no approved treatments.
catalyst_text_evidence: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today announced the submission of its New Drug Application (NDA) to the FDA for oral BBP-418 for the treatment of individuals living with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9). Comprehensive submission includes interim Phase 3 FORTIFY data demonstrating BBP-418's rapid, consistent treatment effect and favorable safety profile, with statistically significant and clinically meaningful improvements in ambulation and pulmonary function. FORTIFY, the Phase 3 clinical trial of BBP-418, successfully met all pre-specified primary and secondary endpoints of its 12-month interim analysis. Additional positive results demonstrating the rapid and consistent treatment effect and favorable safety profile of BBP-418 were presented earlier this month at the 2026 MDA Clinical and Scientific Conference in a late-breaking oral presentation, which can be found here.

catalyst_text: Presented positive long term extension results in cardiomyopathy
detailed_catalyst_text: Long-term efficacy and safety results from the ATTRibute-CM open-label extension through Month 54 were presented for transthyretin amyloid cardiomyopathy. Continuous treatment showed significant reductions in all-cause and cardiovascular mortality versus placebo-to-acoramidis, mitigation of NT-proBNP rise, stabilization of KCCQ-OS, and favorable tolerability. These findings support sustained clinical benefit and reinforce early and continuous treatment in this population.
catalyst_text_evidence: PALO ALTO, Calif., 2026-03-30 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today presented long-term efficacy and safety data from the ATTRibute-CM open-label extension (OLE) trial, demonstrating sustained clinical benefit of acoramidis through Month 54 in patients with ATTR-CM. These data were presented at the American College of Cardiology (ACC) Annual Scientific Sessions & Expo in a late-breaking oral presentation by Prem Soman, M.D., Ph.D. of University of Pittsburgh School of Medicine and it was the only ATTR-CM presentation selected for the ACC late-breaker session. These data are now simultaneously published in JAMA Cardiology. The findings from the OLE trial included: At Month 54, continuous acoramidis treatment led to a statistically significant risk reduction of 44.7% in all-cause mortality (ACM) (p<0.0001) and 49.3% in cardiovascular mortality (CVM) (p<0.0001) versus placebo-to-acoramidis, which is the earliest timepoint in an open-label extension with this magnitude of risk reduction in these events Through Month 54, acoramidis mitigated the rise in NT-proBNP versus placebo-to-acoramidis to an extent not seen in the era of disease modifying treatments Early and continuous acoramidis treatment stabilized and maintained all measures of heart failure-related QOL scores (KCCQ-OS), which demonstrates that the improvement in duration and quality of life in patients with ATTR-CM by acoramidis is sustained Acoramidis continued to be well tolerated with no long-term safety concerns

catalyst_text: Presented positive phase 3 interim data at conference
detailed_catalyst_text: Additional positive interim analysis results from the Phase 3 FORTIFY trial in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 were presented at the MDA Clinical and Scientific Conference. Data showed early separation from placebo on the 100-meter timed test, improvements in ambulation and biomarkers, and a safety profile comparable to placebo. These findings support potential clinical benefit in this progressive neuromuscular disease.
catalyst_text_evidence: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today presented additional positive data from the interim analysis of FORTIFY, the Phase 3 clinical trial of oral BBP-418, in individuals with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9). These data were presented at the MDA Clinical and Scientific Conference in a late-breaking oral presentation by Katherine Mathews, M.D., Professor of Pediatrics and Neurology at the University of Iowa's Roy J. and Lucille A. Carver College of Medicine. BBP-418 demonstrated a rapid time to separation on the 100-meter timed test (100MTT), with improvements in ambulation showing separation from placebo as early as three months post treatment. At 12 months, individuals treated with BBP-418 completed the 100MTT approximately 31 seconds faster than those receiving placebo. BBP-418 was generally well tolerated, with a safety profile comparable to placebo.

catalyst_text: Interim Phase 3 analysis met key efficacy endpoints
detailed_catalyst_text: An interim analysis of the ongoing Phase 3 FORTIFY study in limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 showed that efficacy endpoints were met. This positive registrational signal supports potential clinical benefit in this rare neuromuscular disease. Additional details are slated for disclosure at a scientific meeting.
catalyst_text_evidence: BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. ... announced today that additional data from the interim analysis of FORTIFY, the Phase 3 clinical trial of BBP-418 in patients with limb-girdle muscular dystrophy type 2I/R9 (LGMD2I/R9), will be shared in a late-breaking oral presentation at the MDA Clinical and Scientific Conference, taking place in Orlando, Florida on 2026-03-08 to 2026-03-11. Late-Breaking Oral Presentation: Interim Analysis from Ongoing Phase 3 FORTIFY Study of BBP-418 for Patients with LGMD2I/R9 Meets Efficacy Endpoints

catalyst_text: Phase 3 topline results positive meeting primary endpoint
detailed_catalyst_text: Positive topline data were reported from the global Phase 3 PROPEL 3 study in children with achondroplasia, meeting the primary endpoint of change in annualized height velocity with strong statistical significance. Secondary measures, including height Z-score and an exploratory analysis of body proportionality in younger children, also favored treatment, underscoring clinical relevance.
catalyst_text_evidence: PALO ALTO, Calif., 2026-02-12 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- BridgeBio Pharma, Inc. (NASDAQ:BBIO) ("BridgeBio" or the "Company"), a biopharmaceutical company focused on developing medicines for genetic conditions, today announced positive topline results from PROPEL 3, the global Phase 3 pivotal study of oral infigratinib in children living with achondroplasia. PROPEL 3 successfully met the primary endpoint of change from baseline in AHV at Week 52 (p<0.0001). In a pre-specified exploratory analysis of the key secondary endpoint, oral infigratinib achieved the first statistically significant improvement in body proportionality against placebo in achondroplasia, demonstrating an LS mean treatment difference of -0.05 (p<0.05) against placebo in children younger than 8 years old (>50% of the participants).
